🏠 Building on a slope? Here’s why we step our footings. When a house sits on sloped ground, we use stepped footings to transition with the grade while keeping each section of the footing level. Instead of trying to make up the elevation difference with extra block, brick, and mortar, the concrete footing itself steps down. This gives the mason a solid, level platform to start from, saves unnecessary material, and creates a cleaner foundation from the ground up. It’s one of those details you may never see once the house is finished—but it matters. “For every house is builded by some man; but he that built all things is God.” — Hebrews 3:4 #newhome #contractor #construction #homebuilding #diy
